<note>This passage continues a discussion on the transmutation of metals, focusing specifically on the process of citrination—a yellowing stage in alchemy.</note>
shining citrination, or rather dark and livid with a deadly earthiness.
However, the Moon <note>alchemical term for silver</note> is also citrinated with the solution of Mars <note>alchemical term for iron</note>.
The method of that citrination, which is perfected through Vitriol or Copperas, is as follows. Take a certain quantity of each of these, and let that part which is capable of sublimation be sublimed, until it is sublimed in its entirety by expression. After this, let that which has been sublimed be sublimed again with the mode of fire appropriate to it, so that something of it may be fixed after something else, until the greater part of it is fixed. Afterward, let it be managed with the intention of fire-caution, so that a greater fire may be applied to it for perfection. After this, let it be dissolved into a most ruby-red water, to which there is no equal. Then, you shall devise a way to provide it entry into the Lunar body <note>silver</note>, and these devices have been sufficiently demonstrated to you, if you are a seeker of the perfect work which we have written. And because we see these things adhere amicably to the depth of the Moon, we have therefore considered—and it is certain—that these are of their root, and therefore it happens that they are altered by them. These are indeed all the medicines of the first order which we have brought forth, yet many modes of them can be multiplied, provided the essence of the pigmentary substances remains in the variety of modes. Some have indeed discovered many medicines, but one of two things necessarily happens, because it is necessary that they create the medicine either from the same things, or from things having the same nature. Or they compose a medicine which is equivalent to that which is not, along with its alteration, and which confers nothing to the world, nor to the parts of the world, until the mover has rested incorrupt in the sublime, mobile nature.

<summary>This page describes the alchemical process of citrination using vitriol or copperas to prepare substances for the transmutation of silver, emphasizing the necessity of fixed natures and the consistency of elemental roots.</summary>
<keywords>citrination, alchemy, vitriol, copperas, silver, transmutation, fixation, metallic medicine</keywords>
